verdict: The site passes the 10-second test. The hero, the "Not every business needs every service" act and the audience tabs make it clear what SxBP does, and I found no fabricated proof anywhere. Conversion breaks at the handoffs. The most direct buy signal on the site ("Plan a route with this" on a division page) silently drops the division the visitor just chose. The route builder's last screen says "Your route is ready." before anything has been sent. The pages where intent peaks (/work, every screening, and the bottom of every division page) end without a call to action.

findings.problem: The final screen's h2 is "Your route is ready." while nothing has been sent yet. The stepper calls this step "Send", and the three send buttons sit below a drawn route and a collapsed "Read the brief".
findings.why: "Ready" reads like a confirmation, so visitors may think they are finished and leave. The honest handoff exists in the button hints, but the headline undoes it.
findings.fix: Change it to "Last step: send your route." and add a lede under it: "Pick a channel. WhatsApp or email opens with your brief written; nothing reaches us until you press send there." After an adapter click, change the status (line 200) to "WhatsApp opened in a new tab. Press send there and it reaches us at +91 8432935877."

findings.problem: headingRef.current.focus() scrolls the h2 to the top of the viewport. Because the nav hides on scroll-down, the 5-station progress bar ends up off-screen on every step from 2 to 5, on both desktop and mobile.
findings.why: Visitors lose track of where they are and how much is left in a multi-step form. That is a classic abandonment trigger, and it hides the route-line motif the builder is themed on.
findings.fix: Use headingRef.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true }), then root.current?.scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' }) with scroll-margin-top: calc(var(--nav-h) + 1rem) on the root, so the stepper stays in view. Or make the <ol aria-label="Progress"> sticky inside the card: className="sticky top-0 z-10 bg-petal py-3".

findings.problem: 18 identical outlined "+ ROUTE" pills stack down the right edge of every row, on both home and /capabilities. "Route" alone does not say what it does (add to a shortlist), and the only feedback is a small counter on the nav pill, which is hidden while scrolling down.
findings.why: The persona rule says never ship 10 identical buttons. Here a repeated unexplained control buries the one action that matters.
findings.fix: On md+, hide the toggle until the row is hovered or focused: add `md:opacity-0 md:group-hover:opacity-100 md:group-focus-within:opacity-100` (keep it visible when aria-pressed=true). Relabel it "+ Add to route" / "âœ“ On your route". On the first add, show a toast at bottom-right: "Added {name}. {n} on your route Â· Review â†’" linking to /route.

findings.problem: When validation fails, only red text appears at the bottom, below the textarea. The inputs set aria-invalid but nothing styles it, so the Name and Email fields look unchanged. Only Name is marked required, though one of Email/Phone is also required.
findings.why: Visitors have to read the bottom of the form to find out which field failed, which adds friction at the last data step.
findings.fix: Add `aria-[invalid=true]:border-signal-ink aria-[invalid=true]:bg-signal/5` to the input className. Render each error directly under its field. Change the labels to "Email *" and "Phone / WhatsApp *", with a helper line "* name, plus email or phone". Focus the first invalid field on failure.

findings.problem: Steps 1 and 2 allow Continue with nothing chosen. Step 3 then has no suggestion, the Continue button is disabled at 40% opacity, and "0 on your route" gives no reason.
findings.why: The disabled button has no explanation, so the visitor hits a silent wall.
findings.fix: When route.length===0, render the live text as "Pick at least one division to continue, or go back and choose your business for a suggestion." Alternatively, require an audience on step 1: canContinue[0] = Boolean(audience).

findings.problem: cinema:line-clamp-1 cuts the payoff line to "Use insights, execution and continuous improvement to support sustainablâ€¦" at 1440 wide.
findings.why: The outcome station is the promise of the whole method, and its key word is cut off.
findings.fix: Use `cinema:line-clamp-2` for the body, or shorten the column split: grid template 'what happens' column min 44ch. Keep the detail line clamped.

findings.problem: Each row shows whatItIs[0] clamped to 2 lines. It mostly repeats the title ("Digital Marketing Strategy & Consulting helps businesses understand their current digital position,â€¦") and is cut before the benefit.
findings.why: For a scanner this is filler. It is the spot where specificity should help them pick.
findings.fix: Show the first three sourced deliverables instead: d.deliverables.slice(0,3).join(' Â· ') (for example "Marketing strategy Â· Audit report Â· Competitor analysis"), set as text-sm opacity-70, with no clamp needed.

findings.problem: WhatsApp, the primary channel for an Indian SMB audience, is styled text-muted grey under the phone number, while email is blue. "Visit www.sxbp.com" is unlinked plain text that points to the site the visitor is already on. The footer has no button-weight CTA.
findings.why: Direct contact should always be one obvious tap away, and the most-used channel is the least visible.
findings.fix: Drop text-muted from the WhatsApp link and render it as a pill: `inline-flex rounded-full bg-blue px-4 py-2 text-white`, labelled "Message on WhatsApp â†—". Replace the "Visit" column with a "Plan your route â†’" blue pill linking to /route, or remove it.

findings.problem: The primary CTA "Start your Pilot Route" is brand jargon. Nothing near it says that it means a 1-minute brief sent by WhatsApp or email. The explanation only appears on /route.
findings.why: Visitors click jargon less when they cannot tell the cost of the click.
findings.fix: Add a one-line hint under or next to the hero and finale primary buttons, in `label text-muted mt-2`: "1-minute brief Â· sent by WhatsApp or email".

findings.problem: Clicking "Send by email" sets the status to "Opening emailâ€¦" permanently. On machines with no mail client (common on Windows), nothing happens and there is no fallback.
findings.why: The visitor is left at a dead end at the very last click.
findings.fix: After window.open, run setTimeout(() => setStatus(`No email app opened? Write to ${site.email} or use Copy the brief.`), 2000), and render the email as a mailto link inside the status.

findings.problem: The label "[ 06 ] Who we work with" is hard-coded, so on /approach it shows a stray "06" where no other section is numbered.

findings.fix: Add an `index?: string` prop and render `[ {index} ]` only when it is passed. Home passes "06"; /approach omits it.

top3: Fix the route handoff bugs. Make "Plan a route with this" add the division (routeStore.add or /route?add=slug). Merge suggestions instead of replacing them. Only claim "we've started you with a suggested route" when that actually happened.

Add primary CTA bands where intent peaks: /work, each /work/[slug] ("Want work like this? Plan a route with {its divisions}", pre-filled), and the bottom of every division page. Promote WhatsApp to a button in the footer.

Make the builder's last mile honest and legible. Rename step 5 to "Last step: send your route." with the hand-off lede. Keep the progress stepper in view (focus with preventScroll, or a sticky stepper). Mark invalid fields inline. Sort the drawn route by division number.

verdict: Home is the strongest part of the site. The hero fan, the cornflower manifesto takeover, the marquee with inline reel stickers and the departures board read as one memorable world. The inner pages fall back to a single template (headline on the left, empty right half, no work on screen), and polish slips at the moments that should land hardest: clipped descenders on the /approach H1, a broken finale underline, truncated board copy, an orphaned ticket row and a crushed footer wordmark. The red-and-blue system is executed with discipline. What's missing is the real 9:16 work, which disappears after home, and the "route" metaphor, which never reaches the one page named after it (/route).

findings.problem: With 10 stations the deck lays out 8 + 2, leaving 'Optimize' and 'Scale' orphaned on a second row with 1000px of empty space beside them. Each ticket is also mostly blank white: a 35px header, an empty body, then one word. There is no route line connecting them, so they read as generic small cards rather than boarding passes.

findings.fix: Set cols = steps.length <= 8 ? steps.length : Math.ceil(steps.length / 2) (5+5 for 10). Fill the ticket body with boarding-pass data that is already available: 'FROM' = previous station name, 'TO' = this station, in the label style, and a 2px signal-red route line drawn across the row behind the tickets (DrawSVG on scroll, the same ease as the deal). Raise min-h to 9rem and the station name to clamp(1.1rem,1.4vw,1.4rem).

findings.problem: The page named after the brand's core metaphor is a generic form wizard: a grey dots-on-a-line stepper, white option cards, a blue Continue pill. There is no signal line, departures-board or boarding-pass language anywhere in the flow.
findings.why: /route is the conversion endpoint. It is where 'The Pilot Route' should pay off, and right now it is the most forgettable screen on the site.
findings.fix: Draw the stepper connector as the red signal line, filling with stroke #FF3131 as steps complete (DrawSVG, glide ease), with dots styled as the board's [ 01 ] station markers. In the empty right column above 'Or just talk to us', render a live boarding pass in the ApproachRoute ticket style: FROM = chosen business type, TO = goal, ROUTE = the selected division chips. It updates as the user picks options and becomes the summary on the Send step.

findings.problem: At 1440px the letters collide: O/C/I/A/L in SOCIAL and A/N/D in BRAND overlap into blobs. The wordmark is also inset (â‰ˆx 130-1325), so it is neither aligned to the 56px gutter nor the 'edge-to-edge' sign-off its own comment describes.
findings.why: The footer wordmark is the last frame of every page. Fused glyphs look like a font-rendering bug, not a stencil.
findings.fix: Change tracking to -0.028em, remove the `gutter` padding on [data-word] and size it to the viewport: [font-size:clamp(3rem,16.4vw,19rem)] with text-left and pl-[calc(var(--gutter)-0.04em)], so it bleeds exactly gutter-to-edge. Verify with a probe that scrollWidth equals clientWidth.

findings.problem: The 'one accent word per headline' rule is broken in four places. The footer sets a whole sentence across 3 lines in blue serif italic ('Every audience has something worth connecting with.'). /work italicises 'as it was made.', /capabilities 'not the full menu.' and /approach 'Then everything else.'.
findings.why: The serif accent works because it is scarce. Whole italic sentences flatten the hierarchy and make the display face look secondary.
findings.fix: Keep the copy but italicise one word: footer 'connecting', /work 'made', /capabilities 'mix' (or 'not'), /approach 'everything'. Set the rest of the turn in the display face at weight 600, blue for the footer.

findings.problem: Without a hover (and always on touch), the index is roughly two screens of plain ink rows on shell: number, name, a clamped grey description and a '+ ROUTE' pill. No image, no colour field and no motion appear in the static frames. The cursor reel preview is the only visual, and it is hover-only.
findings.why: This is the longest stretch of the home film with nothing alive in it, between the iris marquee and the departures board.
findings.fix: Add a 56x100 (9:16) thumbnail reel at the left of each row, after the number, on md+. Show it as a poster only, play on row flood, and reuse the preview map already in src/lib/previews.ts. Alternatively, collapse each cluster to 4 visible rows plus 'Show all 11' on home only.

findings.problem: A 475x475 square logo lockup is forced into a 9:16 card with object-fit:cover, so 'SOCIAL CREATOR PIâ€¦' is cut off on both sides.

findings.fix: For photo items with aspect <= 1, use object-fit:contain on a petal (#F3ECE9) card with p-6, or render that card as aspect-square in the masonry.

findings.problem: The poster frame was grabbed mid-motion. The 'Riyansh Ayansh' sign is heavily motion-blurred, so it looks out of focus while every neighbouring card is sharp.

verdict: At 1440 and 1280 the desktop build looks clean, and there is no horizontal overflow on any route or viewport tested. Tablet sizes are where it breaks. At 768x1024 and 1024x768 the hero fan covers the headline, the departures board splits words across rows ("UNDERST/AND"), the ladder labels overlap and the nav wraps. There are also systemic small-scale defects on every viewport: index labels wrap to "[ 05 / ]", serif descenders are clipped by the split-line mask, board copy is truncated with an ellipsis, and many mobile tap targets are under 44px.

verdict: The home pins mostly hold up: the departures board, the strike on the manifesto, the velocity marquee and the finale fill all do what they should. The problems are in execution. Every division page has a ticket "deal" that visibly snaps into place, the marquee freezes whenever you scroll up, and mobile loses the manifesto's key moment while spending a quarter of the page on a sticky word swap. Joins between sections are hard cuts, and the inner pages open on a still half-empty frame. On those pages motion stops being the website.

findings.problem: The deck is never stacked before the trigger starts. Before 'top 85%', tickets 02-10 sit already laid out in their row and only 01 is rotated. When scrubbing begins they jump into the deck, then deal out again. The probe confirms it: at scroll 1700, tickets[1..4].style.transform is empty; at 1800 they are translate3d(-147pxâ€¦) and translate3d(-315pxâ€¦). The cause is a single staggered .from() combined with invalidateOnRefresh. After a refresh invalidates the tween, staggered children that have not started yet are no longer rendered at their from-values.
findings.why: This is the signature motion of every division page, and the first thing the user sees is the cards popping backwards. It reads as broken, not choreographed.
findings.fix: Build one tween per ticket so every 'from' is rendered at time 0, e.g. `const tl = gsap.timeline({defaults:{ease:'none'}, scrollTrigger:{â€¦same}}); tickets.forEach((t,i)=> tl.fromTo(t, {x:()=>first()-t.offsetLeft+i*6, y:()=>tickets[0].offsetTop-t.offsetTop-i*3, rotate:(i%2?5:-5)+i*0.6}, {x:0,y:0,rotate:0,duration:0.5,immediateRender:true}, i*0.04));`. Alternatively, drop `stagger`, since scrub already spreads the motion over time. The y term also fixes the second-row problem below.
findings.evidence: qa-shots/motion-director-div2-1440x900-1700.png (row laid out) vs motion-director-div2-1440x900-1950.png (stacked), plus the debug.mjs transform probe

findings.where: Home Marquee 'WE WILL SHOW / you will grow': src/components/home/Marquee.tsx:26,46,52
findings.problem: Scrolling upward into or inside the band freezes both rows. The repeat:-1 loop tweens run backwards to totalTime 0 and stop there. The probe scrolled up from 11250 to 10170 and both tracks came to rest at x=0 and x=-3715. They did not move during 1s of idle with the band fully on screen, and only restarted after scrolling down again. The loops are also created playing, so they run off-screen from page load until the first onToggle.
findings.why: This band is the brand line in motion, and a 'velocity-driven' marquee that dies on reverse looks broken. Backward scrolling is common: people scroll back to the work rail just above it.
findings.fix: Create each loop with `paused: true` and start it far from zero: `const l = gsap.to(t,{xPercent: fwd?-50:0, duration: fwd?34:48, ease:'none', repeat:-1, paused:true}); l.totalTime(l.duration()*1000);`. Then onToggle play/pause as now. A negative timeScale then never reaches the start. Alternatively, add `onReverseComplete(){ this.totalTime(this.rawTime() + this.duration()*100); }` to each loop.

verdict: The code is in good shape. `tsc` and `eslint` both pass, the GSAP calls are matchMedia-scoped and reverted, the Next 16 params / generateStaticParams / dynamicParams / JSON-LD escaping are all correct, and the view-transition names are unique per page. The problems are at the edges the brief cares about most. With reduced motion, the reel Play button sits inside the card link, so pressing it opens the work page instead of playing the reel. The menu dialog lets keyboard focus fall through to the page behind it. The video budget gives decode slots to invisible ladder layers. At 768 and 1024 wide, layout breaks: the departures board copy is cut to a few words, the hero's intro text is squeezed into a narrow column, and the ticket rows are split or crushed. The footer email collides with the phone number at 1280 and 1440 wide.

findings.problem: Each of the 5 stacked ladder layers mounts an in-view Reel. They all intersect equally, so the budget hands 2 of its 3 desktop decode slots to opacity-0 layers. At step 1, layers 0 and 2 (opacity 0) were PLAYing alongside visible layer 1. release() also never re-ranks, so a video paused for being over budget stays on its poster after a slot frees, until its own IntersectionObserver fires again.
findings.why: Two thirds of the decode budget is spent on video no one can see, which hurts the 'home load cost' item in the handover. The non-resuming budget can leave a visible reel frozen.
findings.fix: Ladder: render `<Reel ref={(r)=>{reelRefs.current[i]=r}} mode="manual" â€¦/>` and in `show(i)` call `reelRefs.current[i]?.play()` and `.pause()` on the others. Gate the play on an IntersectionObserver on the section so nothing plays off-screen. video-budget.ts: move the rank loop into `rebalance()` and call it from both requestPlay and release (after `playing.delete(el)`).

findings.problem: The two loops start playing as soon as they are created. They are only paused from `onToggle`, which never fires until the trigger first becomes active and then inactive. Both tracks were already moving at scrollY=0, about 9 screens above the band, and they keep ticking until the user has scrolled through it once.
findings.why: Every page load runs two infinite transform tweens off-screen, during the hydration window the handover names as the load bottleneck. DivisionTicker already handles this correctly.
findings.fix: Create the loops with `paused: true`. After ScrollTrigger.create add `if (st.isActive) loops.forEach(l => l.play())`, or swap the ST toggle for an IntersectionObserver the way DivisionTicker.tsx:281 does.

findings.problem: Child routes do not set openGraph, so they inherit the root `url: '/'`. Every page emits `og:url=https://www.sxbp.com`, including /work, /capabilities/performance-marketing and /work/restaurant-hospitality, while their canonicals are correct.
findings.why: Social shares of any inner page credit the homepage URL, which weakens the per-division SEO that sitemap.ts sets up.
findings.fix: Remove `url` from the root openGraph. Add a helper `ogFor(path)` to src/lib/seo.ts that returns `{ type:'website', siteName: site.name, locale:'en_IN', url: path }`. Set `openGraph: ogFor('/work')` (and so on) in each page's metadata and generateMetadata; child openGraph replaces the parent object, so the helper must carry siteName and locale.

findings.problem: It has the ARIA tab roles but not the tab pattern. There is no arrow-key, Home or End handling, every tab is in the Tab order (no roving tabindex), tabs have no id, the panel has no aria-labelledby, and `aria-live` on the tabpanel re-reads the whole panel on each change.

findings.problem: DrawSVG runs on paths with `vectorEffect='non-scaling-stroke'` inside `preserveAspectRatio='none'` SVGs. On every home load GSAP warns '<path> length cannot be measured when vector-effect is non-scaling-strokeâ€¦', so the draw lengths are estimates.
findings.why: The signal-line draw can finish early or late, and a console warning shows on every load.
findings.evidence: console on every home probe: 'Warning: <path> length cannot be measured when vector-effect is non-scaling-strokeâ€¦'
findings.fix: Remove vectorEffect and set `strokeWidth` in viewBox units (about 2 for the 1000Ã—80 box), or keep preserveAspectRatio default ('xMidYMid meet') and size the SVG by aspect ratio.

findings.problem: These create one ScrollTrigger per item for one-shot reveals: 3 on home, about 6 per work page for data-rise, and 7 on mobile for the board flaps. HANDOVER Â§6.12 says one-shots go through `observeOnce`.
findings.why: Each extra trigger adds to every ScrollTrigger.refresh(), and home already has three pins.
findings.fix: Replace with `observeOnce(items, REVEAL_MARGIN, (batch) => batch.forEach(play))`. For example, in AiAmplifies build each pair's timeline `paused: true` and call `.play()` in the callback. Keep only the scrubbed data-drift triggers.

findings.problem: The pointerenter and pointerleave listeners are added inside the matchMedia handler and never removed. The cleanup only disconnects the IO, so after a revert or remount the listeners still call `slow()` on killed tweens.
findings.why: It leaks across matchMedia changes and React StrictMode remounts.
findings.fix: Store the handlers and remove them in the returned cleanup, or use `{ signal }` from an AbortController and call `ac.abort()` in cleanup.
